children: An independent watchdog found no reasonable ground to believe that a federal criminal law was violated in the former Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell's handling of the Marriner S. Eccles and 1951 Constitution Avenue NW buildings renovation project.
However, the evaluation did find deficiencies in the management of the renovation project and recommended corrective actions.
In May this year, Kevin Warsh, President Donald Trump's nominee,

in as the 17th chairman of the Fed, succeeding Jerome Powell. Powell had led the central bank for eight years. In an unusual situation, Powell remained on the board while an investigation continued into his handling of renovations at Fed buildings and whether he perjured himself in testimony to Congress.

For the Eccles-1951 renovation project, the Fed board had estimated a cost of $1.317B in 2020, with the construction phase ending by Q2 2024. However, as of August 2026, the project had an approved budget of $2.381B, with the construction phase ending by December 2027.

in January that the Department of Justice had opened a criminal investigation into his handling of the ~$2.5B renovation of two Fed buildings in Washington. He had called the probe intimidation and part of broader efforts to pressure the Fed to cut interest rates.
In April, the Inspector General of the Federal Reserve
the probe as the Justice Department dropped its investigation.

Trump has constantly berated Powell for his stewardship of the Fed. Meanwhile, Powell had said he'll remain on the board while the investigation into his handling of the Fed buildings' renovation continues.

title: Evaluation clears Powell of administrative misconduct in Fed buildings renovation project
